https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/black-c.text: A drunk tenant who threatened his housemate with two kitchen knives at a HMO in Smethwick has escaped jail. Maciej Pelczar, aged 48, became 'drunk and aggressive' in the kitchen of the Rutland Road address in October 2024, a court heard. Shane Kenny, prosecutor for the Crown, said both Pelczar and the victim resided at the HMO where tenants had their own bedrooms but shared the kitchen and bathroom. READ MORE: Birmingham ANPR cameras issue 65 penalty charges for right turn ban in 10 days Get breaking news on BirminghamLive WhatsApp , click the link to join Outlining the case, Mr Kenny said: "On October 3, 2024, Mr Pelczar was drunk and aggressive and had two kitchen knives in his hand which he was threatening the victim with." Wolverhampton Crown Court was told the matter wasn't immediately reported to West Midlands Police . Instead, referencing court documents, His Honour Judge Perry said there was a "repeat incident" on November 25. The victim then complained to his landlord, who contacted West Midlands Police, and officers later visited the address to arrest the defendant. A statement from the victim which was read out to court said: "I have tried to reason with Maciej about his behaviour and demeanour when he is drunk - but he does not listen. "I'm really scared that one day, when he is drunk, he will actually stab me whether that's his intention or not. "It is like walking on egg shells when he is at home and drunk. "I have not done anything wrong to Maciej and don't deserve to feel this way in my own home." James Kumar, defence counsel for Pelczar, said his client was self-medicating with alcohol at the time for paranoia. Mr Kumar said the defendant, who'd previously lost his job, believed people were "spying on him and after him". Explaining why Pelczar had knives in his hand during the incident, Mr Kumar said: "He said he was in the kitchen making food. He is remorseful." The court heard that nine days after the HMO incident, Pelczar was seen with a knife at Tesco . As a result, he was handed an 18-month prison sentence which was suspended for two years in January this year. Discussing the timeline of events with Mr Kumar, Judge Perry said: "The January matters relate to him being on Tesco car park waving a knife around." Mr Kumar replied: "That was on October 12. The one that's being sentenced today is October 3." The defendant previously appeared at magistrates court on June 12 this year, where he pleaded guilty to threatening a person with a bladed article in a private place. The court heard he changed his plea on the day his trial was due to take place, and he was subsequently awarded 10 per cent credit. Pelczar appeared in the dock on Friday, July 10, wearing a blue shirt and pale green shorts, and he was accompanied by a Polish interpreter. The court was told he'd since been moved to alternative accommodation. Addressing the defendant, Judge Perry said: "I'm sentencing you for October 3. "The complainant didn't make a complaint about that at the time. "It was a later incident that he complained about, nearly two months later. "He didn't complain directly to the police, but complained to his landlord and they referred the matter to police. "In between these two incidents, you were convicted of a further offence in January (this year), that fell between these two incidents, and that's what you are serving a suspended sentence for." Judge Perry noted there were "aggravating factors" in the case, namely Pelczar's "alcohol addiction if you can call it an addiction," he said. Judge Perry said the offence was "too serious" to consider a community order, while a custodial sentence wasn't "disproportionate". The judge also said that Pelczar had a history of "good compliance" with his existing suspended sentence order. As a result, Pelczar, of Eastfield Road, Bordesley Green , was handed an 18-month prison sentence, suspended for two years. In addition, he was handed 30 days of Rehabilitation Activity Requirement, 150 hours of unpaid work and a victim surcharge.

https://english.news.cn/europe/20260922/.text: Hungary fines MOL Petrochemicals over safety shortcomings BUDAPEST, Sept. 22 (Xinhua) -- Hungarian authorities have fined MOL Petrochemicals 38 million forints (120,000 U.S. dollars) over safety shortcomings uncovered in an investigation into a deadly explosion at its plant in eastern Hungary in May, according to local news portal Borsod Online. The fine was imposed by the country's occupational safety authority following an investigation into the May 22 accident at MOL Petrochemicals' site in Tiszaujvaros, Borsod Online reported on Monday evening, citing information from the Ministry of Social and Family Affairs. One worker was killed in the explosion. Four others were seriously injured and seven sustained minor injuries, according to the ministry. The investigation found that safety systems in the part of the plant affected by the explosion did not fully meet related requirement, said the ministry. Authorities ordered MOL Petrochemicals to review its safety systems and carry out regular maintenance of pipelines and other equipment. ■ News In-depth Sports Business Culture World China Regions Asia & Pacific Europe Middle East North America South America Africa Organizations Services Weather Live & Work in China Doing Business Investment Visit China Study in China More Special Reports Photos Video Corrections About Us Contact Us Media Qiushi Journal Taiwan.cn Youth.cn GMW.cn CE.cn Ecns.cn China Daily CRI.cn China.org.cn People's Daily

Photograph: Debbie Hill/UPI/Shutterstock First Thing newsletter US news First Thing: US ambassador in rare diplomatic break with Israel over attack on US journalist Mike Huckabee condemns attack on Washington Post photojournalist that has drawn lukewarm response from Israeli authorities. Plus, Japan is attempting to boldly go where no space mission has gone before Martin Belam Mon 19 Oct 2026 07.23 EDT Last modified on Mon 19 Oct 2026 07.24 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Good morning. The US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, has denounced a settler attack that left the Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine badly beaten and needing surgery as a “despicable act of terror”. Levine, 63, an award-winning journalist who lives in Israel, was set upon last Friday by masked Israeli settlers who used clubs and other weapons to attack Palestinian people attempting to harvest their olives. The photographer, who is in hospital recovering from hand surgery, broken ribs and other injuries, said she was beaten for more than 10 minutes. Huckabee said: “We have called for a full investigation, arrest, and prosecution to the fullest extent of the law to whoever participated in this. Attacking a female photographer is despicable act of terror carried out by masked cowards.” What else has Heidi Levine said about the attack? She said: “I was attacked, pushed to the ground. Luckily, I had my flak jacket and helmet, otherwise I probably wouldn’t even be here, because they just kept kicking and kicking me. I’ve been covering this region for over 40 years and I have never seen this country in such a state as it is today. I’ve invested decades of blood, sweat and tears into this. They cracked my bones, they haven’t cracked my spirit.” How have Israeli authorities responded ? In a move Levine said left her “shocked and insulted”, Israel’s prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, has been ambiguous in addressing the assault. He said he condemned “violence against anyone” but referred to the attack as “alleged” and said its circumstances remained unclear. Macron criticises ‘unbridled violence’ after days of unrest and 2,400 arrests across France View image in fullscreen A fire burning in city hall in Limoges, central France. Photograph: Pascal Lachenaud/AFP/Getty Images The French president, Emmanuel Macron, has criticised “unbridled violence” after one of the most violent days of unrest in years left public buildings burned, hundreds of shops destroyed and looted and at least 2,400 people arrested in cities across the country. Macron said “nothing justifies” violence and that local state officials would be able to ban certain street gatherings if they deemed it necessary. Macron condemned the “failures” he said had led to the crisis, but he refused the resignation of the interior minister, Laurent Nuñez. What is causing the wave of protests across Europe? School conditions, housing costs and the cost of living have brought demonstrators on to the streets in several countries including Spain, France and Portugal. Protests in Albania against the prime minister, Edi Rama, entered their sixth day on Sunday. Demonstrators there have said they are unhappy with perceived corruption, a lack of jobs and poor education standards. US gave us no warning of Russian strikes on Kyiv power plants, Zelenskyy says View image in fullscreen Aftermath of a Russian missile attack in Kyiv. Photograph: Valentyn Ogirenko/Reuters Ukraine did not receive a warning from the US about an impending Russian missile attack on Sunday evening, Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said, reviving concerns that Washington is withholding intelligence in order to bully Kyiv into capitulating to Moscow. On Friday, Donald Trump waived a sweeping package of sanctions on Russia. Ukraine has also complained of slowed deliveries of air defence missiles from the US. Zelenskyy wrote in a social media post: “When the supply of missiles for Ukrainian air defence is blocked, and Russia receives sanctions relief or delays, it is, unfortunately, a denial of reality on the part of our partners.” Obama condemns comments by ‘border tsar’ that Ilhan Omar could ‘of course’ be denaturalized View image in fullscreen Homeland Security officers carry boxes from the Washington residence of Rep Ilhan Omar. Photograph: J Scott Applewhite/AP Barack Obama has condemned comments by Donald Trump’s “border tsar” that the Republican presidential administration could “of course” strip the Democratic congresswoman Ilhan Omar of her citizenship and deport her. Obama wrote: “The full weight of the federal government is being brought down on a law-abiding elected official because she has dared to criticize the president.” He urged all Americans to defend Omar, regardless of their political beliefs. Flydubai captain describes blocking axe blows as co-pilot attacked him View image in fullscreen The pilot Smit Machchhar. Photograph: Israel foreign ministry/AFP/Getty Images The captain of a flydubai flight who was attacked by a co-pilot who intended to crash the plane has described ⁠blocking axe blows to his head and screaming for help as he reached to open the cockpit door. Capt Smit ⁠Machchhar has been hailed ⁠as a ​hero for his role in averting disaster on the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv last month, helping to thwart what the UAE ⁠attorney general has said was an attempted suicide attack by the co-pilot who intended to crash the plane into Ben Gurion airport. The Australian MP Helen Haines is in critical condition after a suspected attack outside her office. Reports suggest she was deliberately targeted with a vehicle. A CBS reporter has apologized and deleted a post praising someone who heckled Abdul El-Sayed. The Democratic Michigan US Senate candidate had been asked: “Will you disavow the Muslim Brotherhood?” The Roman Catholic church has upheld the excommunication of a Louisiana deacon who resigned from the clergy after a priest molested his son. Amelia Earhart researchers have left a remote atoll empty-handed after suspected “plane debris” was found to be a clump of trees . Photograph: Andrej Ivanov/AFP/Getty Images This month’s biodiversity summit in Yerevan, Armenia, aims to push governments to meet the 23 targets agreed at Cop15 in 2022. Patrick Greenfield explains what you need to know. Last Thing: Japan to launch world-first mission to collect samples from Martian moon View image in fullscreen Phobos, one of Mars’s moons. Photograph: NASA/AP Japan is to launch a spacecraft on the world’s first mission to bring back samples from Phobos . Scientists hope the mission, which is expected to take five years, will provide clues to how Phobos and its smaller sibling Deimos formed, and hopefully even shed light on the origins of life in the solar system.
